The auditor reviews a finished audit before sealing it: what no program can decide, such as whether the summary says what the results show. This command keeps the record of that review, pre-seal.yaml in the audit folder, which seal requires.

The first run writes the checklist: one item per thing to check, each with what it asks (the codeflower-audit skill's references/pre-seal.md says how). Give every item a status there: ok, fixed (with a note: what you fixed) or n/a (with a note: why it does not apply). Run it again when all have one: if the audit is otherwise ready to seal, it records which audit.json, report and pipeline archive were reviewed. When one of them changes afterwards, check again what the change touches and run it once more.

The record is sealed with the audit, in provenance/session.json.


## Usage

```sh
codeflower audit review [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir string` | `audit` | the audit folder (paper.yaml, targets.yaml, consistency.yaml) |
